taxonomic_note: Accepted species. Native in the United States only in far southern Texas near the Mexican border; not native in the current Central Texas target zone.
look_here_first: Look for the mostly unlobed to shallowly toothed, leathery evergreen to semi-evergreen leaves. The acorn cup is deeper than in Shumard oak and may enclose roughly half the nut.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew accepts Texas as native, but Flora of North America describes the U.S. occurrence as a small natural grove about 30 km from the international border. No exact native target-zone counties were established in this review.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Planted Central Texas trees do not count toward native-range qualification.

best_field_traits: evergreen to semi-evergreen oak in cultivation
leaves usually unlobed or shallowly toothed rather than deeply lobed
cup hemispheric to funnel-shaped and relatively deep
cup may enclose about half the nut
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use as a common landscape comparison against local native oaks; do not interpret planted Central Texas specimens as native occurrences.
